# Warlock: engine vs client spell conformance

Client build: 1.60.1.70009. Generated by sim/conformance (FOREVER_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./sim/conformance/...).

Comparison rules: cost (amount and type: client's cost_type 0/1/2/3 = mana/rage/focus/energy vs the engine's core.CostType, both mapped to a shared name; a rage cost is divided by 10 before comparing, since the client stores rage costs in tenths — Bloodthirst's client cost of 300 is 30 rage, Execute's 150 is 15 — while mana and energy costs are already in player-visible units; a spell the client prices as a percentage of base mana — spellconst cost_pct, from SpellPower.PowerCostPct, with a flat cost of 0 — is compared as that percentage of the preset character's base mana, the same amount the engine's ManaCostOptions.BaseCost resolves to, and the percentage is printed beside it); cooldown (client's cooldown_ms, or category_cooldown_ms when cooldown_ms is 0 — spellconst.Spell.EffectiveCooldownMS — vs the engine's Spell.CD.Duration); cast time (cast_time_ms vs Spell.DefaultCast.CastTime; a negative client cast_time_ms, seen as exactly -1000000 on ranged Hunter abilities, is the client's own sentinel for "instant, gated by ranged weapon speed" rather than a literal duration, and is not compared); GCD (gcd_ms vs Spell.DefaultCast.GCD); required level (spell_level vs Spell.RequiredLevel); duration where the spell has one (duration_ms vs the engine's RelatedSelfBuff or Dot aura duration). `match` is every field equal; `client-scripted` is every field but duration equal, where the client states no duration (0, a "server-side script" value in this build's own wording) and the engine keeps a known non-zero value; anything else that differs is `mismatch`, with the Diff column naming every field that does not agree.

Every preset below is built with an EMPTY talent string (see sim/conformance/build.go's buildForComparison): no row in the "Spells" table reflects a talent's cost/cooldown/cast-time/GCD modifier, only the engine's own base registration against the client's base spellconst entry. A spell that does not exist at all without a talent (Seal of Command, Ice Lance, Lava Burst, Stormstrike, Mutilate, and the rest TalentGatedSpells names) is therefore absent from that table and instead reported, with one point spent in just that talent, in its own "Talent-gated spells" section below it.
